notes: Identity independently checked: supplied canonical text contains the title How Quick Decisions Illuminate Moral Character, Clayton R. Critcher, Yoel Inbar and David A. Pizarro, DOI 10.1177/1948550612457688, Social Psychological and Personality Science 4(3), 308–315, copyright 2012; these match the neutral reference. Document is the primary journal article with abstract, experiment methods/results, discussion and references, not a secondary summary or preregistration. Supplied text lists a PDF provenance URL; no PDF path supplied, so no PDF rendering or acquisition performed. Target study/scenario/outcome match Experiment 1, but critical-test identity remains ambiguous. PDF p. 2 reports the moral-decision main effect F(1,117) = 127.07, p < .001; PDF p. 3 separately reports Decision × Speed interaction F(1,117) = 127.07, p < .001, and simple speed effects for immoral decisions t(54) = 8.28, p < .001 and moral decisions t(63) = 7.71, p < .001. The identical printed F values do not establish test correspondence. All are candidates, not selected targets. Canonical simple-effect evidence: t(54) ¼ 8.28, p < .001, whereas quick (vs. slow) moral deci- ... sions prompted more positive moral character evaluations, ... t(63) ¼ 7.71, p < .001 (see Figure 1). Study-level N = 119 is retained only as a candidate, not promoted to analytic N; no arithmetic or df-based N derivation. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders only.
